chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'When the hoods that are left behind (or neglected) appear, adultery will appear.'

key_terms.الْقَلَانِسُ: Hoods or headgear, often referring to a type of cap or turban.
key_terms.الْمُتَرِّكَةُ: The left behind or neglected; implying those that are abandoned or characteristic of a specific era.

ai.seo_question: What does the appearance of 'al-qalanis al-mutarrakah' signify in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, 'al-qalanis al-mutarrakah' refers to the Qalanis, a specific type of hooded cloak worn by the Quraysh in pre-Islamic and early Islamic times; its 'neglect' or change in style is interpreted by scholars like Al-Majlisi as a subtle indicator of shifting social norms and the erosion of traditional modesty. This hadith establishes a causal link between visible changes in attire and broader moral decay, specifically the prevalence of zina (adultery/fornication). It serves as a prophetic warning that external markers of identity and piety, when altered or abandoned, often precede internal spiritual decline.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said:
‘Amir Al Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When the hoods appear as legacy, the adultery would appear’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
’Amir al-Mu’minin has said, ‘When al-Matrakah (a certain kind of cape) becomes public, so also will become fornication.’”
